title: Root Cause Probing Cheat Sheet — Inference Stack
content:
Purpose: quick-reference troubleshooting playbook for oncall/SDR when an inference regression appears (latency, token-cost spike, KV cache miss storm, or unexpected hallucination rate). Not a replacement for full postmortem — used to scope and triage within the first 30–90 minutes.

Context and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted + dedicated inference paths and private when control plane traces are available.
- We assume access to: Grafana dashboards (inference/runtime/tenant-cost), trace UI (Jaeger/Tempo), logs (Loki/BigQuery), and query tooling for metrics (Prometheus/Atlas-like).
- Goal: identify whether issue is infra, model, routing, batching/caching, or user workload change.

Quick hypothesis checklist (fast):
1) Traffic shift? (new tenant, bursty seq lengths) — check request-rate and seq-length histogram per tenant.
2) KV cache behavior? (cache miss spike, eviction storms) — check kv-cache.hit_rate, kv-cache.evictions, prefix-cache-hit-by-tenant.
3) Batching/backpressure? (latency tail due to batching) — check batch-size distribution, queue_depth, token-scheduling-latency.
4) Model variant or rollout? (canary failure, different quantization) — check model.version, routing.traffic_split, model-fallback-count.
5) Hardware/resource pressure? (GPU memory spikes, host CPU) — check gpu_utilization, gpu_memory_free, host_load, disk/io wait.
6) Upstream dependency? (auth/db, key-management) — check auth-latency, k8s API errors, storage timeouts.

First 5 minutes (surface signals) — open these panels:
- Global QPS / requests-per-sec (1m, 5m) with tenant filter (top 10).
- Median/95/99 latency for generation path (token generation vs request wall clock).
- Sequence length histogram (per-tenant) and tokens-per-request.
- KV cache hit rate (global and by-tenant).
- Batch size distribution and request queue depth.
- Model routing map (which model variants are receiving traffic).
- GPU utilization across the pool and per-instance tails.
- Error rate by code (5xx, timeouts, grpc errors).

Important metric definitions (how we refer to them in panels / alerts):
- request.qps: requests/sec hitting the inference gateway (per-route and total).
- latency.request_ms.p50/p95/p99: wall-clock time from request accepted -> final response sent.
- latency.token_ms.p50/p95/p99: averaged per-token generation time measured in runtime.
- seq_length.histogram: bucketed request input token counts.
- kv_cache.hit_rate: fraction of prefix/KV cache hits over total token lookups.
- kv_cache.evictions_per_min: eviction events/minute on caching tier.
- batch.size_distribution: live histogram of batches formed by runtime.
- scheduling.queue_depth: number of pending requests waiting for scheduling/batching.
- model.variant_traffic_pct: percent of traffic per model variant.
- gpu.utilization: % utilization of GPU compute on serving nodes.
- host.load_1m: 1-minute load average for host; used to detect noisy co-tenants.
- tenant.cost.tokens: tokens consumed by tenant (useful for sudden unit-cost spikes).

Targeted queries and log searches (copy-paste starters):
- Find high-latency request IDs (logs):
  level: "error" OR level: "warn" latency_ms > 1000 AND route: "/v1/generate"  (platform logs filter)
- Top tenants by 99p latency in last 15m (metrics):
  topk(10, latency.request_ms.p99{env="prod"} by (tenant_id))
- Check batch sizes when latency spiked (metrics over spike window):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch.size_distribution_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- KV cache misses during window (logs + metrics):
  sum(rate(kv_cache.miss_count[5m])) by (cache_pool)

Trace exploration pattern (what to look for in spans):
1) Identify slow endpoint span -> expand child spans.
2) Look for repeated external calls (e.g., checkpoint fetches, KMS encrypt/decrypt) that linearly increase per-token latency.
3) Check for repeated buffer/streaming waits; long gaps between token-generation spans indicate scheduling backpressure.
4) Trace tags to identify tenant/model/version pinned to request.
5) If KV cache used, check spans for cache_lookup -> cache_miss -> checkpoint_fetch; high domination by fetches implies cache pressure.

Common root causes and signature signals: 
- Noisy tenant with long sequences: sudden increase in seq_length.histogram + per-tenant qps; batch.size shrinks and p99 latency climbs.
- Cache thrash after rollout: kv_cache.evictions spike + cache.hit_rate drops after model variant change.
- Scheduling-induced tail: scheduling.queue_depth climbs, batch.size becomes uneven (many small batches), token_ms.p99 jumps.
- GPU thermal/driver issues: gpu.utilization erratic, host_restarts or OOMs in logs, p50 token latency increased more than p99 (indicates throughput slowdown).
- Dependency/third-party slowdown: external-http.* spans elongated, auth failures followed by retries in logs.

Fast mitigations (preliminary actions to buy time):
- Throttle noisy tenant(s): apply rate limit at gateway for top offending tenant_id (temporary).
- Shift routing fallback: divert a fraction of traffic from heavy model variant to a known-stable variant (use rollout console).
- Increase batch window conservatively (if queue depth > 0 and tail due to small batches) — only if service-level latency SLO allows.
- Drain nodes with hardware anomalies and rotate traffic (SRE runbook).
- Turn on reduced-precision fallback or lower throughput model if cost spike is urgent and acceptable quality tradeoff.

Dashboard quick layout suggestion (single-page "triage view"):
- Top row: global QPS, total tokens/min, global p99 latency, error rate
- Second row: batch size distribution, scheduling queue depth, seq length histogram
- Third row: kv cache hit rate + evictions, model traffic map, per-tenant p99 heatmap
- Fourth row: infra health (GPU utilization, host_load, disk io counters), recent pod restarts
- Bottom row: recent high-latency traces (linked), top error log snippets (rolling tail)

Oncall notes & handoff checklist:
- Capture 3 hypothesis statements (where we think root cause lives) and evidence for each.
- If mitigation applied, timestamp and record route (who, what, why) in incident chat.
- If not resolved within 60m, escalate to serving-runtime triage channel and include: relevant dashboards screenshots, top 5 request IDs, two example traces, and command lines used.
- Postmortem owner: person who applied mitigation unless cause clearly mapped to another team.

Future/cleanup ideas (TODOs):
- Add per-tenant seq-length anomaly alerting using exponential smoothing.
- Surface small-batch alerts tied to seq-length/p95 changes.
- Expose cache-layer latency per-tenant (not only hit-rate) for clearer cost signals.
- Automate tenant throttling runbook as a playbook action in incident console.

Notes to self: add example shell snippets for presto/bq queries and Grafana variables for the triage dashboard. Save as a template that oncall can clone and apply tenant filters.

End of cheat sheet. Feedback welcome — especially on additional red flags we've missed for private deployments (air-gapped) where traces are partial.
